text:
maya_vp: Thanks everyone for joining the runtime deep-dive. Spawning this live thread for leftover questions and quick follow-ups. Keep it short and we'll assign owners.

jordan_runtime: Quick Q: what should teams expect from default batching configs for Hosted vs Dedicated moving forward?

sam_engineer: Current defaults: Hosted uses adaptive batching with max_batch_tokens=4096 and target_latency_ms=50. Dedicated leans heavier: max_batch_tokens=8192 and target_latency_ms=80. Those are baseline and can be overridden per-route.

elena_ml: We're seeing tail latency on long-context models (32k). Any roadmap notes?

jordan_runtime: Kernel squad is prototyping sequence-aware kernels that can early-stop unnecessary attention work for padding-heavy requests. Aim to test canary in Q2.

ryan_sre: For SLOs, is the plan to attach them to models or routes? We need to hook alerts.

maya_vp: Final plan: Console will expose per-route SLOs, but you can inherit model-level defaults. Alerts will be configurable per-route. Shipping per-route SLOs next console release.

claire_prod: Prewarm vs on-demand guidance? PLG apps are worried about reserved capacity costs.

sam_engineer: Short: prewarm for latency-sensitive low-throughput routes; on-demand autoscale for bursty PLG endpoints. Use cache TTLs to hide cold-starts, and set soft prewarm thresholds to reduce wasted capacity.

ops-bot: autoscaler: updated policy applied to pool-2 at 14:12 UTC :white_check_mark:

jordan_runtime: KV cache question: what's our eviction heuristic today?

elena_ml: We use a heuristic-LRU that prefers prefixes seen in last 24h; planning to add a sticky-prefix window for multi-turn agent sessions.

sam_engineer: Example tunables:
```
cache.max_items=200000
cache.prefix_sticky_window=4h
cache.eviction_policy=heuristic-lru
```

claire_prod: Who's responsible for the kernel v3 rollout and what are the gates?

jordan_runtime: Kernel team leads rollout. Plan: 5% canary -> 20% -> 100%. Rollback gates: 95th percentile latency, token error rate, and QA regressions. I'll post a detailed playbook.

maya_vp: Action: jordan to publish rollout playbook plus target metrics by Friday EOD. @jordan_runtime

jordan_runtime: On it. :thumbsup:

ryan_sre: Request: add a "cost cap" per-route metric in Console so Product can prevent runaway spend.

claire_prod: Also want visibility for effective quantization level (int8/int4) per deployed model in the UI.

maya_vp: Noted. Product + Console to prioritize; we'll triage in roadmap sync Monday.

sam_engineer: Will new quant profiles default to int8 or int4?

elena_ml: Default is int8. auto-int4 will be enabled only after perf/quality validation on compatible architectures.

ops-bot: incident-bot: created alert rule kernel-latency-95th > 400ms :bell:

ryan_sre: Can Applied ML publish an ordered fallback table (accuracy vs latency vs cost) for model families? Teams want predictable degrade paths.

maya_vp: Yes, we'll have a draft table next week. Applied ML to own it.

claire_prod: UX ask: can we get a "dry-run" canary mode to validate correctness without impacting routing?

jordan_runtime: We have router flag dry_run=true — inference executes but traffic routing/metrics are not affected. I'll add Console toggle.

maya_vp: Thanks all. Post PRs/docs into this thread if you have them; closing after EOD unless there are blockers. :eyes:

sam_engineer: Prewarm guide: https://redwood.internal/docs/prewarming-guides

elena_ml: Draft sticky-prefix doc: https://redwood.internal/notes/cache-sticky-prefixes

jordan_runtime: Rollout runbook posted: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kernel-v3-rollout

claire_prod: Leaving +1 and adding a test case in the prod tests.
